newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy telecoms bill possible without hardleft-govt.
newsitem.headline: Italy telecoms bill possible without hardleft-govt.

text.p: The Italian government could get a bill, which covers the creation of a watchdog authority for the telecoms sector, approved in parliament without the help of hardleft Communist Refoundation, the cabinet secretary said.
Approval of the bill is needed before state telecom holding Stet can be privatised but the legislation is being held up by Refoundation which is ideologically opposed to the planned sell-off.
Asked by reporters if the bill could be approved without Refoundation backing, cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli replied: "Technically speaking, yes."
Asked if such a much would be politically acceptable, Micheli said: "We want to approve the watchdog...Refoundation has to make its choice."
The hardleft Refoundation guarantees the government's majority in the lower house of parliament and has held talks with Prime Minister Romano Prodi in recent days over the telecoms issue.
Further talks are due before the end of next week.
The Public Works Committee in the upper house of parliament, facing a wave of amendments, suspended work on the telecoms bill last month.
The Committee was due to resume examination of the bill later on Wednesday, but parliamentary sources said the session would be suspended if no political compromise was sighted.
